Good web design in Midland, TX has a job most towns never ask of it: keeping up with the Permian Basin. When oil climbs, crews are hard to find, rents rise and the dinner rush runs late. When it falls, the same owners trim hours, chase new kinds of work and need their customers to know it right away. A site that takes a month and a developer to edit is a liability here.

Dominion Web Design Pro is Maurice Johnson, a Texan who writes every page by hand from Big Sandy in East Texas. You see a free demo built for your business first, then decide. The prices are fixed and paid once: $497, $997 or $1,997.

A town that moves with the barrel

Midland's economy leans hard on oil, and its small businesses ride the cycle closely. The Dallas Fed's report for mid-2024 is a good recent picture: Permian oil output hit a record 6.2 million barrels a day in the second quarter, yet the region ran 36 fewer oil rigs than a year earlier (310 in June against 346) and nonfarm jobs shrank at a 1.4% annual rate through June. Record production and fewer jobs can happen at the same time, and that gap lands on the payrolls, lunch counters and apartment complexes around town.

Older swings were sharper. In the 2015 slump, a New York Times report from Midland found a Mexican restaurant adding Sunday brunch to widen its sales and a car dealer shifting toward repairs and used cars. In 2020 a price war and the pandemic hit together, a pairing CBS News called a double whammy for the city. Owners here learn to adjust their offer quickly; the website has to adjust with them.

Five edits a Midland site should handle in an afternoon

Think of these as the switches on the wall. Each one should be a quick message to Maurice, not a rebuild.

  1. Hiring on, hiring offA short careers section with the roles you need, the pay range if you want to show it and a simple way to apply. In a tight labor market it may be the most visited page you have. When the market loosens, it comes down without leaving a dead link.
  2. Hours that match realityShort-staffed weeks, a closed Monday, a later opening. The site and your Google Business Profile should change together so nobody drives across Loop 250 to a locked door.
  3. A service you are pausing or addingSlower months often mean new kinds of work: residential jobs for a commercial contractor, catering for a restaurant, mobile service for a shop. Each deserves a clear paragraph, not a line buried on the home page.
  4. A plain notice at the topOne line for a holiday closure, a move, a weather delay or a waitlist. Visitors see it before anything else.
  5. Prices or minimumsIf you publish them, they should move when your costs move. If you do not, the site should say how to get a quote and how soon you answer.

Where Midland customers come from

Shoppers and diners concentrate along Loop 250, especially the stretch between Midland Drive and Garfield Street, where restaurants and shopping centers line the road and Midland Park Mall sits off the Midkiff Road exit. Office workers fill downtown during the week. Then there is the airport: Midland International Air and Space Port is owned by the City of Midland and sits inside city limits about halfway between downtown Midland and downtown Odessa. In 2014 the FAA licensed it for commercial spaceflight, the first primary commercial service airport in the country to receive that license, according to the airport.

That geography matters for search. Google says local results depend on relevance, distance and prominence. A business near the airport may serve both cities; a clinic downtown may draw mostly from its own side of town. Your pages should say plainly where you are and how far you go, so Google and the customer reach the same answer. If you also cover Odessa, our Odessa page shows how that city's businesses differ.

Local help that costs little or nothing

  • UTPB Small Business Development CenterRun through the University of Texas Permian Basin's College of Business, with Midland and Ector among the counties it serves. It won a 2024 Excellence and Innovation award from the Northwest Texas SBDC network. Good for business plans and financing questions before you spend on marketing.
  • Midland Chamber of CommerceMore than 1,000 members, the Leadership Midland program it has run since 1978, and Founder's Blend, a free Wednesday morning networking and program hour for entrepreneurs (its August 2026 newsletter lists August 5).
  • Midland Development CorporationThe city's economic development arm. It has funded small business work through UTPB, including a $200,000 payment under an incubator and makerspace grant agreement with the university, and it backed the Midland Entrepreneurial Challenge, which offered up to $100,000 each to as many as eight winners when it relaunched in 2021. Check its site for what is open now.

Common questions

How much does web design in Midland, TX cost?

Quotes in any town run from a few hundred dollars to several thousand, and some come with a monthly fee that never stops. Ours are printed: Starter is $497, Pro is $997 and Agency is $1,997, each paid one time. Hosting, maintenance and updates are $49 a month, or included while you keep one of our AI agents. Ask any designer you talk to for the first-year total in writing so you can compare honestly.

Can you change my site quickly when we start hiring or cut hours?

Yes. Updates are part of maintenance, so you send the change (a new opening, Saturday hours dropped, a service paused) and Maurice makes it. We also build the pages so those pieces sit in obvious places, like a hiring section that can be switched on or off without redesigning anything.

Do you work with oilfield service companies or only shops and restaurants?

Both kinds of business fit. A service company needs its capabilities, coverage area, safety program and a way to request a bid; a restaurant or salon needs hours, a menu or price list and one-tap calling. Maurice asks how your customers buy before he writes anything, and the pages follow that.

Will my Midland site also show up for people in Odessa?

It can, if you really serve Odessa. Google weighs relevance, distance and prominence, so a page that honestly describes the work you do in Odessa, Ector County or out toward Andrews helps searchers there find you. We will not write pages for towns you do not serve.

Is Dominion Web Design Pro based in Midland?

No. Maurice Johnson is a Texan in Big Sandy, East Texas, and he builds every site remotely. There is no Midland office. Call (903) 636-7511 any hour; an AI receptionist answers and can put you through to Maurice.
